$comment: The shrink-only ::part() ratchet (#71, C-007).
ADR-11 item 6 says every ::part() the MANIFEST declares must be present and targetable.
That is the right mechanism and #72-#74 inherit it — but today it is vacuous: the manifest
declares 0 cssParts, so a 'derived expected list' is a green assertion over nothing.
This file is the anti-vacuity guard. Adding a ::part() without updating it — and therefore
without a test — fails CI. Removing one is allowed and shrinks the count. Same shape as
check-manifest-content.mjs: derive from the source of truth, refuse to pass vacuously.
#72 is the first growth this ratchet has had to gate: <sk-card> declares part "card",
recorded here in the same PR as the test that targets ::part(card) — which the ratchet now
requires, not merely assumes.
#73 grows it again: <sk-nav-pill> declares nav, items and hamburger, each recorded here in
the same PR as the [SC-013] test that targets it from outside and the mutation that proves
that test goes red. The ratchet's known looseness is unchanged and still recorded: a mention
inside a comment or a test.skip() satisfies the source scan, and it is not scoped per element.
#74 adds five for <sk-form-input>. Note the @csspart JSDoc is what populates the manifest —
a lens shipped eight part= attributes with an empty cssParts array and this ratchet stayed
green at the old count, because it derives from the manifest and not from the rendered DOM.

#77 adds one for <sk-grid>: part "grid". A layout primitive's variants are a closed set, so the part is the only route a consumer has to a column count or gap the element does not offer — recorded here in the same PR as the [SC-013] test that targets it from outside.

#77 adds three for <sk-section-banner> (banner, dot, label). <sk-site-footer> is deliberately not here — it is held out of this batch, see issue #77. Each is targeted from outside by the [SC-013] test in that element's own fixture file. Note what the RATCHET can and cannot hold: check-part-ratchet.mjs scans the concatenated test sources for the literal `::part(<name>)`, so it is not scoped per element — `::part(label)` already appears in three other files, and deleting section-banner's own label case would leave the ratchet green. `banner` and `dot` are currently unique and so are genuinely bound. The per-element binding is a property of the tests as written, not something this file enforces.

#78 adds two for <sk-feature-card>: card and chip. `chip` is the accent surface — the accent set is closed, so the part is the only route to one outside it, the same argument sk-grid's `grid` part carries.

#78 adds three for <sk-ribbon-card>. Note `ribbon` is ABSENT from the DOM on a plain card — the element renders `nothing`, not an empty div — so its [SC-013] case mounts a card that has one, and a separate assertion covers the absence.

#79 adds FOUR across its three components, and an earlier revision of this note said 'adds one' while the data below added all four — the identical note/data asymmetry #78's note two lines up already records being caught for. <sk-button>: `button`, the rendered <button> or <a>, one part because that node is its whole surface. <sk-check-bullet>: `bullet` and `icon`. <sk-pill-tag>: `tag`. total moves 23 -> 27.

#78 adds three for <sk-blog-card>: card, content and thumbnail. `card` carries BOTH `sk-card` and `sk-blog-card` — the composition ruling means one root, so one part covers the frame both sheets style. `thumbnail` is absent from the DOM when no thumbnail is set, so its [SC-013] case mounts one that has it.

#77 adds FOUR for <sk-site-footer>: footer, grid, divider, legal. Total 30 -> 34. Each is a SHADOW node — the component's own surface — which is exactly why they are the parts: everything a reader sees is slotted and therefore already the consumer's to style. `grid` is the escape hatch for a layout outside the provided `1.5fr 1fr 1fr`, the same argument sk-grid's `grid` part carries. Naming all four here rather than one, because three separate gates have now caught a note claiming a different number than its own data.

#146 WP01 adds ELEVEN parts across section-header (six), status-indicator (three) and entity-marker (two), each with a literal external selector and computed-style assertion. On the consolidated train-based mission target, total moves 69 -> 80.
#146 WP02 adds EIGHT sk-action-row parts: row, trigger, marker, title, reference, tags, metadata and controls. Total moves 80 -> 88.
#147 adds FIVE sk-metric parts (metric, label, value, annotation, empty-state) and FOUR sk-evidence-chain parts (list, stage, connector, empty-state). Total moves 88 -> 97.

#178 adds sk-notice with SEVEN parts — the largest single entry here, and deliberately so: a notice is a composition (marker, heading, body, actions, dismiss) rather than a single box, and under-exposing parts is the support burden ADR-9 §2 names. Every one is targeted from outside by the [SC-013] test in fixtures/elements-behaviour/src/sk-notice.test.ts, which is what the ratchet scans for. `body` is also the live region, so a rename there is an ANNOUNCEMENT regression as well as a styling one.
#148 WP01 adds SEVEN sk-bar-chart parts: chart, plot, item, bar, value, label and empty-state. On the refreshed train after #147 and #178, total moves 104 -> 111.

#179 adds sk-time-series-chart's SIXTEEN parts, total 111 -> 127. Three of them are the mission's own subject rather than ordinary styling surface. `gap` is a DRAWN OBJECT — the mutation that interpolates across nulls removes it, so the [SC-013] test's red is a part's ABSENCE, the shape sk-card's #177 arm records; that is why the [SC-013] fixture mounts a series WITH an interior null run rather than only a dense one. `point` exists only when the chart is selectable, so its fixture is the selectable mount. `gap-note` and `gap-notes` exist only when a SUPPLIED gapThreshold is met, so their fixture supplies one — an element that inferred a threshold would render them unconditionally and the ratchet would never notice.

#212 adds only sk-action-row's supporting part, backed by its focused external-targetability test and SC-013 mutation. On the refreshed train after #179, total moves 127 -> 128; every other element part set is unchanged.
#254 adds sk-app-shell compact-header and compact-navigation as two externally targetable parts, total 128 -> 130. The six legacy parts remain unchanged.
#257 adds sk-copy-field's four stable surfaces (field, value, copy-control, status), each present in its SC-013 fixture. On the refreshed train after #254, total moves 130 -> 134.

#308 adds sk-confirm-dialog with SIX parts: dialog, title, body, actions, cancel, confirm. Each is targeted from outside by the [SC-013] test in fixtures/elements-behaviour/src/sk-confirm-dialog.test.ts. Total moves 134 -> 140.
